# Slop Game Research

How quick AI-built Roblox games are picked, made, promoted and paid, from creator videos and press. Researched 11 Nov 2026.

**Read this first:** almost everything here is creators' own claims from auto-generated transcripts of their videos. Several of these creators sell courses or are sponsored by the tools they show. None of the earnings figures are verified.

How to build each of these genres well is in [[20 - Slop Game Blueprints]]; this note is the market side.

## What a "slop" game is

- A cheap, fast copy or remix of a trending game, usually built with AI tools in days.
- Roblox says 70,000 games were published in five months with AI tools (press report). Roblox Studio now has agent tools that build from text prompts.
- Favoured genres, per one creator: quiz, clicker and simulator, because they are quick to build.
- Players forgive rough polish if the game is playable and the theme is in demand (creator claim).

## How they pick the game

- **Find demand with weak supply.** Search a fantasy (airport, firefighter, cleaning) in Roblox's Creator Exchange or a tracker such as RoTrends, sort by visits, and look for many players across few or poor games.
- **Check demand off Roblox.** Steam wishlists and web-game view counts for the same fantasy.
- **Reuse a mechanic a hit already proved.** Test question: "Does a popular Roblox game already share a mechanic with this game?"
- **Change about 20%** of a proven map or loop; keep the rest.
- **Avoid brand-new fantasies with no demand**; one creator calls them "very, very risky".

## The trend cycle

Three phases, per the first video you linked:

1. **First to market.** The original takes most players.
2. **Saturation.** Clones flood in and sink to low player counts (one cited at 31 players).
3. **Mutation.** Survivors change the title, thumbnail and add a twist (fishing became ice fishing and cage fishing).

The factory should enter at phase 1 or go straight to mutation. Phase 2 is where copies die.

## Why clones get no traffic

- Roblox's docs say games whose listing and place files closely resemble existing ones are deprioritised in recommendations and may rank lower in search (creator citing official docs; matches [[02 - Engagement Playbook]]).
- The creator's best-performing thumbnail was fully original, not a copy of a popular one.
- **So: never publish from an unchanged template, and never copy a title or thumbnail.**

## How they build

One documented workflow (creator sponsored by the tool he used):

- Claude connected to Roblox Studio through a third-party connector.
- Blender driven by its scripting interface for models.
- A four-minute reference video of the target game, then "ask me questions" prompts, then several reference images per model.
- Image generators for the icon.
- Built in days. Another creator built a 2,000-player game in "3 to 4 days".

## Icon and thumbnail

- Icon with no text, cartoony, one clear subject. Text was removed in a later pass and click rate improved (creator claim).
- Original art outperforms copied art.

## Ads

One creator's numbers for a new game at about 16 ad credits a day:

| Day | Impressions | Clicks | Visits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 43,000 | 770 | 410 |
| 3 | 87,000 | 1,604 | 923 |

- Click rate about 1.8%. Roughly half of clicks became visits.
- Total spend quoted as 7,000 to 10,000 Robux.

## What makes the money

- One 2,000-player game: 1.39 million Robux over 56 days, about $3,800 a month. **Nearly all from repeatable products; passes "made nothing".** Top seller was a "Nuke All" product used in play.
- One AI-made cleaning game: about 40,000 Robux a day, about $4,000 a month (third-party estimate).
- A 21,000-player game: creator claims about $131,000 a month.
- Reference shop screenshots: random eggs in packs of 1, 3, 10 and 50.
- Bulk-buy buttons (buy 1, buy 3, buy 10) were added after playtests in one game.
- Median creator payout across Roblox was about $1,500 over 12 months (press, citing Roblox). Most games earn little.

## Keeping one alive

From a creator running a 21,000-player game:

- Weekly update, launched Saturday. Sunday plan, Monday to Wednesday build, Thursday ready, Friday playtest with 8 to 10 testers.
- Watches days played per player, bounce rate and playtime per player.
- Reads bug reports and Roblox's feedback summary; watches competitors.
- "Don't prioritize monetization over gameplay."

## What this changes in the factory

- **Idea step added:** demand-versus-supply check before any build. See [[06 - Marketing Playbook]].
- **Products matter more than passes.** The standard shop needs repeatable in-play products. See [[03 - Monetization and Shop Standard]].
- **Every game needs its own title, thumbnail and one twist**, even on the shared skeleton.
- **Portfolio view:** several games on one loop with different themes is what these creators do. Expect most to fail the day-14 gates in [[00 - Start Here]].
